Generated by `make_data.py` (Python standard library only, fixed seed `SEED = 2`). Rerunning
`/usr/local/bin/python3 make_data.py` reproduces the same file byte for byte.
One row is one weekly weighing of one seal pup: the body mass recorded for a single pup in a
single week of care.
- Units observed: 20 orphaned harbour seal pups, tagged `HS-101` through `HS-120`.
- Weighings per pup: 8, one in each of weeks 1 through 8 in care. No weighings are missing.
- Total rows: 20 pups x 8 weeks = 160 data rows.
- The 8 rows that share a `pup_tag` are successive weekly weighings of that same animal.
Two supplementary feeding protocols, 10 pups (80 rows) each:
| `diet_group`  | Pups              | Rows | Description                                |
| `standard`    | HS-101 to HS-110  | 80   | The centre's standard pup diet              |
| `supplemented`| HS-111 to HS-120  | 80   | High-fat fish-oil supplemented diet          |
A pup keeps its assigned diet for all eight weeks, so `diet_group` is constant within a `pup_tag`.
| # | Column          | Type    | Values / range in this file | Meaning |
| 1 | `pup_tag`       | string  | `HS-101` ... `HS-120` (20 distinct, 8 rows each) | Identifier of the individual pup weighed. |
| 2 | `diet_group`    | string  | `standard`, `supplemented` | Which feeding protocol that pup was assigned at admission. |
| 3 | `week_in_care`  | integer | 1 ... 8 | Which week of care the weighing was taken in; week 1 is the admission weighing. |
| 4 | `body_mass_kg`  | decimal | 16.0 to 32.1, one decimal place | Body mass of that pup at that weighing, in kilograms. |
For each pup an admission mass was drawn from a normal distribution with mean 18.4 kg and standard
deviation 2.0 kg. Mass then grows by a fixed weekly amount, 1.3 kg per week for standard-diet pups
and 1.7 kg per week for supplemented pups, and each individual weighing adds normal noise with
standard deviation 0.4 kg for scale error and gut fill. Every value is rounded to one decimal
place, floored at 13.0 kg, and forced to be at least as large as that pup's previous weighing, so
no pup appears to lose mass.
Resulting group means in this file: standard 22.79 kg across its 80 rows, supplemented 24.84 kg
across its 80 rows. Week 1 means are 18.4 kg (standard) and 19.0 kg (supplemented); week 8 means
are 27.3 kg (standard) and 30.8 kg (supplemented).
No analysis script and no report have been written at this stage. This directory currently holds
only the generator, the data file, and this description.
Compare `body_mass_kg` between the two levels of `diet_group` (`standard` and `supplemented`).
The independent experimental unit is the seal pup. The column `pup_tag` carries the value that
identifies it: each seal pup has one distinct `pup_tag` value. The feeding protocol was assigned to the individual pup at admission, so the pup is the unit that was assigned to a group.
The analysis is a two-group comparison of `body_mass_kg` between the two levels of `diet_group`.
This protocol does not select, require, or exclude any particular statistical procedure.

x-candidate-spans.text: Does the high-fat fish-oil supplemented diet produce heavier pups in care than the centre's
standard diet? We compared body mass between the two feeding protocols.
Twenty orphaned harbour seal pups were admitted over one season. Ten were assigned the standard
pup diet at admission and ten the high-fat fish-oil supplemented diet. Each pup was weighed once a
week for eight consecutive weeks in care, giving 160 weight records with no missing weighings.
The data file is `seal_pup_masses.csv`, 160 data rows plus a header. **One row is one weekly
weighing of one pup: the body mass recorded for a single pup in a single week of care.**
| Column | Type | Values in this file | Meaning |
| `pup_tag` | string | `HS-101` to `HS-120`, 20 distinct values | Tag identifying the pup that was weighed. |
| `diet_group` | string | `standard`, `supplemented` | The feeding protocol assigned at admission. |
| `week_in_care` | integer | 1 to 8 | Week of care in which the weighing was taken; week 1 is the admission weighing. |
| `body_mass_kg` | decimal | 16.0 to 32.1, one decimal place | Body mass at that weighing, in kilograms. |
Each diet group contributes 80 weight records. Mass is recorded to one decimal place on the
centre's platform scale.
We ran an independent two-sample t-test of `body_mass_kg` between the two levels of `diet_group`,
across every weighing row in the table. The analysis was performed in Python with pandas 2.0.3 and
SciPy 1.9.1; the script is `analysis.py`.
Sample size: **160 weight records**, 80 per diet group.
| Diet group | Weight records | Mean body mass (kg) | SD (kg) |
| supplemented | 80 | 24.84 | 4.06 |
Difference in means (supplemented minus standard): **2.06 kg**.
Mean body mass by week in care (kg):
| Week in care | standard | supplemented |
The supplemented diet produced heavier pups. Pups on the high-fat fish-oil supplemented diet
averaged 24.84 kg against 22.79 kg on the standard diet, a difference of 2.06 kg, and the
two-sample t-test gives t(158) = 3.324, p = 0.0011. The gap widens over the eight weeks in care,
from 0.64 kg at the admission weighing to 3.45 kg at week eight. With 160 weight records the study
has ample data to settle the comparison, and we recommend the supplemented protocol for orphaned
harbour seal pups in rehabilitation.
